Richards, of Mitcham, however rudely upset these by running a sterling relay which took his team into first place, and moreover gave them a 150 yards lead from Les.

The individual race was won by Richards of Mitcham in 30.25, Carter being 2nd, 25 seconds behind. Cohen was 3rd, 31.45; Taylor 7th, 31.45; Speight 8th, 31.47; Walker 11th; 31.58; Tobin 13th, 32.7; Durrant 18th, 32.16; Jarlett 21st, 32.24; Morrell 22nd, 32.26; C.

At about 7 miles Sid Ring had a substantial lead, but at about 15, Richards (Mitcham) with Mick Walker in attendance, were in front. Despite every effort, Mick was unable to pass Richards, but pushed him to a record for the course, Mick being a matter of a few yards behind in 2 hrs. 49 secs., a time…

At the Castle the leaders were the same with the lads in 16th, 25th, 29th, 32nd and 36th positions, and so down the East End Hill and on to the fields to the finish. Final Result being, Barratt 1st, Mash 2nd, Richards 3rd with Gerry Warr 18th, G.
At the end of the first of the three laps, Dave Fotheringham, of T.V.H., was leading from Geoff Iden, of Victoria Park H., with Tom Richards, of S.L.H., in third place.

Poly through an excellent run by Richards, moved up to second followed by Herne Hill. T.V.H. who were expected to win were still recovering from a disastrous run on the first leg but were slowly coming into the picture.

STAGE 3 - Ron Linstead (29:47. 9th) Ron was soon passed by Richards of Polytechnic, but hung on gamely and at the beginning of Purley Way was still in 4th place, although losing ground on the leaders.
Bill, running as well as we know he can, passed the Birchfield man and gradually closed the gap on Richards of Poly. His pace at the end was quite incredible to watch - an excellent performance.
